title: Bug: "HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor" crash when using Vertex AI with HTTP_PROXY environment variables

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear report of a runtime crash (TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor) when using Vertex AI authentication with proxy environment variables set. Detailed environment details, error log, root cause analysis, and reproduction steps are provided.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The issue has a clear root cause and requires a localized fix in two esbuild patch files (`packages/cli/src/patches/https-proxy-agent.ts` and `packages/cli/src/patches/http-proxy-agent.ts`) by adding default exports to complement existing named exports, along with updating test assertions.

summary.problem: When running Gemini CLI with Vertex AI authentication and proxy environment variables set (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY), execution fails with 'TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor'.
summary.root_cause: The patch files aliased by esbuild (`packages/cli/src/patches/https-proxy-agent.ts` and `packages/cli/src/patches/http-proxy-agent.ts`) only export named exports (`export { HttpsProxyAgent }`). When dependencies like `gaxios` or `google-auth-library` dynamically import or require the module expecting a default export or constructor, the import evaluates to the module object rather than the constructor function.
summary.context: Gemini CLI aliases `https-proxy-agent` and `http-proxy-agent` in `esbuild.config.js` to custom patch files to handle code splitting and CJS/ESM bundling. Ensuring both default and named exports exist in the patch files allows both default import (`import HttpsProxyAgent`) and named import (`import { HttpsProxyAgent }`) semantics to work seamlessly after esbuild bundling.

steps: In `packages/cli/src/patches/https-proxy-agent.ts`, import `HttpsProxyAgent` from `../../../../node_modules/https-proxy-agent/dist/index.js` and re-export `HttpsProxyAgent` as both a named export and default export (`export default HttpsProxyAgent`).

In `packages/cli/src/patches/http-proxy-agent.ts`, import `HttpProxyAgent` from `../../../../node_modules/http-proxy-agent/dist/index.js` and re-export `HttpProxyAgent` as both a named export and default export (`export default HttpProxyAgent`).

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When bundling the CLI with esbuild, both named exports (`HttpsProxyAgent`, `HttpProxyAgent`) and default exports (`default`) exist on the imported proxy agent modules and can be constructed without throwing errors.
verification_steps: Update `scripts/tests/proxy-agent-bundle.test.ts` to assert that both default export (`https.default`, `http.default`) and named export (`https.HttpsProxyAgent`, `http.HttpProxyAgent`) exist and are constructor functions.
Verify that constructing instances via both default and named constructors succeeds without throwing 'TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor'.
Run `npm run test` or `npx vitest run scripts/tests/proxy-agent-bundle.test.ts` to confirm test suite passes.
